battle.name: 秦滅楚之戰
battle.brief: 西元前225年，秦王政以王翦為主將，率六十萬大軍攻楚，與主將項燕所領二十萬眾戰於鄢、蘄南一線。秦軍深壁高壘、斷其糧道，待楚軍糧盡而潰，乘勝追擊，楚軍大敗。卡面的科林斯青銅盔屬希臘，比本役早五百餘年，並不在楚地戰場；它代表青銅時代全封閉防護的老路，秦軍頭上已是皮冑與弩機的時代。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭是秦王政滅六國序列的最後一步，形式上分成兩段：前225年王翦率主力擊潰楚軍主力，前223年王賁、蒙武追亡逐北，掃清楚王遷的殘餘政權。秦方由關中樞紐調兵，兵源包含關中本籍、新滅的韓魏趙降卒與北方邊郡的騎兵，編制上以王翦總攝，車兵為中堅、騎兵分列兩翼、步兵結大陣，弩手列於陣前，糧秣自關中經漢水、丹水一線轉運，以牛車與駃騠馱載。秦方將領除王翦父子外，另有蒙武、李信與昌平君各領一路。李信前次以二十萬眾伐楚敗績，正是本次改用六十萬的理由之一。楚方是六國中疆域最大的一國，國都郢在今湖北荊州一帶，淮河與漢水以南尚有廣土，兵源以楚地鄉兵與丹陽、藍田一帶的精兵為主，統轄楚王與令尹、將軍之下的宮中政令體系。楚國在殘存階段仍保留完整的官僚與封君架構，項燕為全軍主將，唐蒙在漢中方向修築藍田、鄢間長城以阻秦軍深入。戰前郢一帶已有楚人請降於秦，說明楚國朝堂對秦並非鐵板一塊，軍心與政令從來不同步。
countriesEn: This war was the last step in the sequence by which King Zheng of Qin destroyed the six states, and it ran in two stages: in 225 BC Wang Jian led the main army and broke the main body of the Chu army, and in 223 BC Wang Ben and Meng Wu pursued the fugitives and cleared away what was left of King Qin's government. The Qin side drew its troops from the hub of Guanzhong; the manpower included native soldiers of the capital region, surrendered men from the recently fallen states of Han, Wei and Zhao, and cavalry from the northern frontier commanderies. Its organisation put Wang Jian in overall command, with chariots as the core, cavalry on the two flanks and infantry massed in great formations and crossbowmen ranged in front, while grain and fodder were moved out of Guanzhong along the Han and Dan river lines on ox-carts and on tuotuo pack animals. Besides Wang Jian and his son, the Qin commanders included Meng Wu, Li Xin and Changping Jun, each leading a separate column; the defeat suffered the year before by Li Xin, who had marched on Chu with 200,000 men, was one of the reasons why a force of 600,000 was now considered necessary. The Chu side was the largest of the six states by territory. Its capital Ying lay in what is now southern Hubei, broad tracts south of the Huai and the Han rivers were still in its hands, and its manpower came from the local levies together with the picked troops of Danyang and Lantian. It was governed through the royal court, with the lingyin and the generals issuing orders through the palace administration. Even in its reduced state Chu kept its full bureaucratic and fief structure, with Xiang Yan as commander-in-chief of the whole army, and Tang Meng building a wall between Lantian and Yan in the Hanzhong direction to bar the Qin road into Chu. Before the campaign the people of the Ying region had already petitioned Qin for surrender, which shows that the Chu court was never a single block: the mood of the troops and the orders of the government had never moved together.
people: 秦方核心是三個人。國君秦王政在滅韓、滅趙之後面對的最大問題是楚國太大、太遠、兵太多，他先採王翦之議，仍保留了以大軍壓制的選項，前226年王翦、桓齮已取鄂渚、進軍鄢地，迫近楚北；前225年批准王翦率六十萬出關，楚方在北面失守後曾遣使求和，最終仍批准全軍進攻。主帥王翦是白起之下秦國第二個能獨力滅國的將領，他反覆陳述非六十萬不可，並要求其子王賁留後押運糧道，以免重演李信孤軍深入而潰的舊事；王賁接令領後軍與糧道，前223年正是由王賁、蒙武窮追楚王遷於平與、召陵一線。蒙武奉秦命與王賁分道追擊；昌平君名列《史記》所載秦將，滅楚一役在秦方諸將之中，滅楚之後奉命鎮守新置的楚地郡縣；李信則是前線的失敗者，他以二十萬眾伐楚被項燕擊破，殘軍僅以身免，敗後由楚地逃回，直接證明楚軍不可小覷。楚方領袖項燕是項梁之父，以二十萬眾對峙秦軍，兵敗之後被楚王遷懷疑而殺，死後楚軍失去統帥而崩潰；楚王遷本人在國破之際退保於陳，收攏殘兵再戰，最終兵敗被俘，國祚至此而絕。項燕之子項梁收拾殘眾於江東，楚地反秦的種子由此埋下，相傳韓信等楚地少年即出自這一批隊伍。
peopleEn: Three men stand at the centre of the Qin side. The sovereign, King Zheng of Qin, faced the largest remaining problem after the fall of Han, Zhao and Wei, for Chu was vast, remote and armed with more men than any state left; he followed Wang Jian's advice and kept the option of overwhelming the enemy with massed troops, and in 226 BC Wang Jian and Huan Yi had already taken Ehu and advanced to Yan, pressing close to northern Chu; in 225 BC he approved Wang Jian's march with 600,000 men out of the passes, the Chu side sent envoys to seek peace after its northern screen had fallen, and in the end he approved the full advance. The commander, Wang Jian, was the second Qin general after Bai Qi able to destroy a state single-handedly; he argued repeatedly that fewer than 600,000 would not do, and he required that his son Wang Ben stay behind to escort the supply route, so that the old mistake of Li Xin's unsupported advance into the interior would not be repeated. Wang Ben took charge of the rear guard and the logistics, and it was he and Meng Wu who drove King Qin down the line of Pingyu and Shaoling in 223 BC. Meng Wu was ordered to pursue in parallel with Wang Ben; Changping Jun is named among the Qin generals in the Records of the Grand Historian, took part in the campaign on the Qin side, and was afterwards set to hold the newly created commanderies in the Chu country; and Li Xin was the defeated man of the earlier phase, whose 200,000 were broken by Xiang Yan, who got away with only the remnant of his force and escaped back from Chu, proving that the Chu army could not be dismissed. On the Chu side the leading figure was Xiang Yan, father of Xiang Liang, who faced Qin with 200,000 men; after his defeat he was suspected by King Qin and put to death, and the army lost its commander and came apart. King Qin himself, with the state collapsing, fell back on Chen, gathered what was left of his troops and fought again, and was finally beaten and taken prisoner, which ended the state. Xiang Liang then gathered the survivors on the Jiangdong side, and the seed of Chu's later resistance against Qin was planted in that force; it is said that young men of Chu such as Han Xin came out of those ranks.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔約製於西元前650年前後，是希臘重裝步兵的標準頭部防具：整片青銅面甲開成一條窄眼縫，兩側垂下護頰，額前留冠飾槽，盔脊縱貫頂心。戴上它的人看不見左右，轉頭要靠整個身體，所以它從來不是個人裝備而是隊形裝備，這正是卡面那句話的來處。要把這頂盔放進秦滅楚的戰場，必須老實說明：它並沒有出現在鄢、蘄南的戰場上，比這場戰爭早約五百五十年，而且即使在它的故鄉，到前225年也早被淘汰——希臘世界在前五世紀已改用科斯式與阿提卡式的開放面頭盔，讓戴者能看見側翼。楚地是青銅的故鄉，銅綠山、鄂州、隨州的礦冶與冶鑄傳統深厚，銅器技術在楚並不陌生，但實戰中楚軍的頭部防護仍以皮冑為主，楚式長盾與柳葉形劍才是身體防線的核心。秦軍方面，秦陵兵馬俑坑出土的成束三棱箭鏃、銅弩機、長援鐵戈、柳葉形鐵劍、青銅鍪與皮冑札甲，勾出這一代楚戰場上真正的頭頂與手裡。弩機是秦軍遠射的骨幹，弩手成排，前排蹲下上弦、後排立射，輪番齊發，萬人方陣靠的不是個人技藝而是整體的射速；車兵居中衝撞，騎兵兩翼包抄，步兵持矛戈在盾牆縫隙中直刺鉤啄。攻城一側有雲梯、撞車與封鎖打援的手段，後勤靠牛車運糧，沿途設亭燧與傳舍接應，關中經漢水、丹水轉運的糧秣供應數十萬大軍。楚軍則以弓弩居高、大盾列陣、水軍控江漢之流。兩軍裝備的差距不在單件兵器的貴賤，而在數量與配合。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card was made around 650 BC and was the standard head protection of the Greek heavy infantry: a single bronze face-piece pierced by a narrow eye-slit, with cheek-pieces falling at the sides, a slot for a crest at the brow and a ridge running along the crown. A man wearing it could not see to left or right and had to turn his whole body to look aside, so the helmet was never an individual piece of equipment but a formation piece, which is exactly where the sentence on the card comes from. To set this helmet on the field of Qin's destruction of Chu, one has to say plainly that it never appeared at Yan or south of Qi: it preceded this war by about five and a half centuries, and even in its own homeland it had been obsolete by 225 BC, since the Greek world had moved on to the open-faced Coan and Attic helmets in the fifth century BC, letting the wearer see his flank. Chu was the homeland of bronze; the mining and casting traditions of Tonglushan, Ezhou and Suizhou were deep, and bronze technology was by no means foreign to Chu. Yet in the field the head protection of the Chu army was still leather caps, and the core of the Chu body armour was the long Chu shield and the willow-leaf sword. On the Qin side, the bundled trilobate arrowheads, bronze crossbow triggers, long-hafted iron dagger-axes, leaf-shaped iron swords, bronze helmet caps and leather-and-lamellar armour excavated from the pits of the First Emperor's mausoleum show what actually sat on the head and in the hands of the men who fought over Chu. The crossbow was the backbone of Qin's shooting power, archers ranged in rows with the front rank crouching to reload and the rank behind firing standing, taking turns in volleys; a formation of ten thousand depended not on individual skill but on the rate of fire of the whole body, chariots charged in the centre, cavalry enveloped the flanks, and infantry drove spear and dagger-axe through the gaps of the shield wall. On the siege side there were scaling ladders, rams and the means of sealing roads and cutting off relief, while the logistics ran on ox-carts with beacon towers and relay stations set along the route, the grain and fodder shifted out of Guanzhong along the Han and Dan rivers feeding a force of hundreds of thousands. The Chu army used bows and crossbows from high ground, large shields in line and war boats to hold the Han and Huai waterways. The gap between the two armies in equipment lay less in the value of any single weapon than in numbers and in cooperation.
tactics: 秦滅楚的戰術核心不是一次會戰，而是一場以時間換勝的消耗與封鎖。王翦到軍之後，採《史記》所記的持重之態：壘壁堅固、閉門不出、不理楚軍挑戰，絕不是怯戰，而是六十萬眾必須先整訓成可以整體移動的大陣，同時不給楚軍以逸待勞的機會。楚軍求戰不得，糧秣漸盡，兵食俱困，被迫向東退卻；秦軍這才出壁追擊，在蘄南、鄢下追上潰兵，大破之。楚軍崩潰的直接原因除了饑餓，更有一個關鍵的指揮層面：項燕戰歿後，軍中失去可以服眾的統帥，隊形在追擊與退卻中斷裂，項梁父子只收得數千殘部往江東去。楚軍本身的戰術並不弱：依托鄢、蘄的城垣與險阻，弓弩手居高臨下以矢石壓制秦軍前陣，步卒以長盾結陣，楚式長戈、鉤矛在近身糾纏中佔上風，水軍沿漢水、淮水遲滯秦軍側後；問題在於後方被切斷，前225年楚王已派唐蒙在漢中修築長城，本意是守住入楚的通道，結果反而把秦軍引進了漢中這條進攻走廊，配合秦軍封鎖漢水下游，令楚軍首尾不能相顧。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the campaign that destroyed Chu was not a single pitched battle but a war of attrition and blockade fought with time as the weapon. When Wang Jian reached the front he took the position that the Records of the Grand Historian describes as deliberate: he walled in his camp, shut his gates, met no challenge and did not answer the Chu provocations. This was not cowardice; a force of 600,000 had first to be drilled into a great formation that could move as one body, and meanwhile he was careful not to let the Chu army rest and meet him at their convenience. Denied battle, the Chu troops ran out of food, their supplies and their stomachs were both exhausted, and they were forced to withdraw eastward. Only then did the Qin army come out of its lines to pursue them, catching the routed men south of Qi and below Yan and crushing them. The immediate cause of that collapse was not hunger alone but above all a problem of command: after Xiang Yan fell, the army lost the leader it would obey, the line broke apart during the pursuit and the withdrawal, and the two Xiang could gather only a few thousand survivors to carry east to Jiangdong. The Chu tactics themselves were not weak. Leaning on the walls and broken ground of Yan and Qi, the Chu archers and slingers held the high ground and swept the Qin front with arrows and stones; the foot soldiers closed up behind long shields, and at close quarters the long Chu dagger-axes and hooked spears had the better of it; war boats moved along the Han and the Huai to hang on the flanks of the Qin march. The problem was that the rear had been cut off. In 225 BC the king of Chu had already sent Tang Meng to raise a wall in Hanzhong, meaning to hold the corridor into Chu, and in doing so he handed the Qin army that very corridor, which, together with the Qin blockade of the lower Han, left the Chu forces unable to support one another.
data: 兵員是這場戰爭最硬的數字。楚軍主將項燕所領二十萬眾，見於《史記·楚世家》與《白起王翦列傳》；秦軍主帥王翦自關中領兵六十萬，見於同書《白起王翦列傳》，秦廷議事時以非六十萬不可，王翦力主其數。六十萬對二十萬，是秦國在兼并戰爭中第一次投入如此大的兵力，也是它能一次性壓垮楚國的底氣。前一次敗仗的規模同樣有據：前225年李信將二十萬伐楚，被項燕擊破，殘軍僅以身免。時間軸上，前226年秦已取鄂渚、進軍鄢地，前225年大軍出關，前224年楚軍主力在鄢、蘄一線崩潰、項燕死，前223年楚王遷於平與、召陵一線兵敗被俘，前222年秦置黔中郡，滅楚工程才算收尾。地理距離方面，秦軍自關中出發，經武關、藍田，越秦嶺、漢水，前鋒距郢都僅數百里；糧道自關中經漢水轉運，軍隊在前線停駐待糧的時間以月計，所以王翦寧可先壁壘不動，也不肯在糧道未穩時冒險出戰。死傷與俘虜的精確數字史書不載，只說楚軍大潰、追亡逐北；兵馬俑坑所出箭鏃成束堆放，也說明秦軍消耗的物資是以車載計算的。
dataEn: The size of the armies is the hardest of the numbers in this war. The 200,000 men commanded by the Chu general Xiang Yan are recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian, in the Hereditary House of Chu and in the Biography of Bai Qi and Wang Jian; the 600,000 troops that Wang Jian led out of Guanzhong are recorded in the same book, where the debate at court turned on the figure of 600,000, with Wang Jian pressing for that number. Six hundred thousand against two hundred thousand was the first time Qin had committed so large a force in the wars of annexation, and it was the reserve that let it crush Chu in a single stroke. The scale of the earlier defeat is equally attested: in 225 BC Li Xin marched on Chu with 200,000 men, was broken by Xiang Yan and got away with only the remnant of his force. The chronology runs as follows: in 226 BC Qin had taken Ehu and advanced to Yan; in 225 BC the main army came out of the passes; in 224 BC the main body of the Chu army collapsed in the Yan and Qi area and Xiang Yan died; in 223 BC King Qin was beaten at Pingyu and Shaoling and taken prisoner; and in 222 BC Qin established the commandery of Qianzhong, which closed out the work of the campaign. As for distances, the Qin army left Guanzhong through the passes of Wuguan and Lantian, crossed the Qinling range and the Han river, and brought its vanguard to within a few hundred li of the capital at Ying; the supply line ran from Guanzhong along the Han, and the army's halt in front of the enemy waiting for grain was measured in months, which is why Wang Jian preferred to sit behind his walls rather than risk an advance before his supply line was secure. Exact casualty and prisoner figures are not preserved; the record says only that the Chu army collapsed and was pursued. The arrowheads found in the pits of the terracotta army, bundled and stacked, likewise show that the stores the Qin army consumed were counted in cartloads.
cause: 滅楚是秦王政二十餘年兼并的收尾，背後是四層壓力。其一是六國格局本身的崩解：韓、趙、魏次第覆亡後，楚成為替秦的唯一大國，長期坐擁淮漢之地與百萬之眾，不滅楚就無從統一。其二是楚國體量帶來的治理難題：楚地遼廣、宗室封君的勢力盤根錯節，縣制在楚推行不順，越地、漢中、黔中一線的統治成本極高，秦廷需要一個可以示範的先例。其三是戰略上的必須：前226年王翦、桓齮取鄂渚、擊楚軍於鄢，楚國北面屏障已失，郢都以南門戶洞開，此時不進，等於把主動權還給楚。其四是前次敗績帶來的教訓——李信二十萬眾伐楚而敗，讓秦廷明白楚軍並非弱旅，必須以傾國之力一擊而定。楚國這邊的起因則更直接：楚王遷在國勢傾覆之際，既依賴項燕的二十萬大軍，又對這支兵力的首領心存猜忌；朝中另有人建議割地求和，郢一帶的楚人甚至請降於秦，說明楚國在內部已經分裂成求和與死戰兩條路，而兩條路都在加速它的崩解。
causeEn: The destruction of Chu was the closing of a campaign of more than twenty years under King Zheng, and behind it lay four kinds of pressure. First, the collapse of the six-state order itself: after Han, Zhao and Wei had fallen in turn, Chu was the only great state left, it had for long held the lands of the Huai and the Han with a population in the hundreds of thousands, and without Chu there could be no unification. Second, the difficulty of governing an empire of Chu's size: its territory was vast, the power of its royal clan and feudal lords was tangled and hard to root out, county administration did not take hold in Chu, and the cost of ruling Yue, Hanzhong and Qianzhong was extreme, so the Qin court wanted a precedent it could point to. Third, the strategic necessity: in 226 BC Wang Jian and Huan Yi took Ehu and struck the Chu army at Yan, the northern screen of Chu was gone and the capital at Ying lay open, and to stop then would have handed the initiative back to Chu. Fourth, the lesson of the previous defeat, for the ruin of Li Xin's 200,000 showed the Qin court that the Chu army was no pushover and that the state had to bring everything it had for a single blow. On the Chu side the cause was more immediate: as the state collapsed, King Qin both depended on the 200,000 men of Xiang Yan and feared the man who led them, and there were voices in court urging him to cede land and seek peace; people in the Ying region even offered to surrender to Qin, so that Chu had already split between the party of peace and the party of last stand, and both hastened its dissolution.
impact: 楚亡是秦統一的最後一塊拼圖。前221年秦王政稱帝，齊國同年降秦，六國至此盡滅；但楚地的消化遠比滅楚本身更長。滅楚大軍旋即轉用：蒙恬北擊匈奴，尉繩南征百越，兩路都用同一套秦軍編制與後勤體系，而這些兵馬的技術底子正是在滅楚的六十萬大軍裡練成的。制度上，秦於楚地置黔中郡，後再置楚郡、九江郡、會稽郡、長沙郡，把楚地數百年的封君與世襲特權收進郡縣；秦廷隨後禁私學、收兵器、廢六國舊政，並「墮壞名城」以斷天下人以城自守的念頭，十二萬戶天下豪富被徙於咸陽，數十萬民眾被徵發北遷南調，徭役與兵役的重壓在楚地最先引爆反抗。文化上，楚地沒有被抹去：楚辭、巫風、兵器紋飾與漆器工藝隨著楚人遷徙散入帝國各地，長沙馬王堆的漆器與絲綢展示出楚地工藝的高度，秦陵兵馬俑坑出土的楚式長矛、柳葉劍與青銅鍪則記錄了楚地金屬工藝留在秦軍裝備裡的痕跡。反秦的火種也在楚地埋下：前208年項梁、項羽再起於江東，前207年巨鹿之戰楚軍於野戰中重拾主動權，那支軍隊與那份仇恨正是項燕種下的。
impactEn: The fall of Chu was the last piece in the puzzle of Qin's unification. In 221 BC King Zheng took the imperial title and Qi submitted in the same year, and with it the six states were wholly gone; but the digestion of Chu territory took far longer than the conquest itself. The armies of the campaign were immediately turned to other uses: Meng Tian drove the Xiongnu in the north and Wei Ling went south against the Baiyue, and both columns used the same organisational system and logistic machine, whose technical foundations had been forged in the 600,000-strong army that destroyed Chu. Institutionally, Qin set up the commandery of Qianzhong in the Chu lands and later those of Chu, Jiujiang, Kuaiji and Changsha, pulling centuries of feudal lords and hereditary privilege into the county-and-commandery order; the court then forbade private learning, took in arms, abolished the old institutions of the six states, and levelled famous cities so that no one would think of holding out behind walls, twelve myriad households of the wealthy of the realm were moved to Xianyang, and hundreds of thousands of men were conscripted and shifted from north to south, with the strain of corvée and service falling hardest on Chu. Culturally, Chu was not erased: the Songs of Chu, its shamanic customs, the ornament of its weapons and the craft of its lacquerware travelled with the Chu people across the empire, the lacquer and silk from the Mawangdui tomb in Changsha showing how high that craftsmanship stood, while the Chu-style spears, willow-leaf swords and bronze helmet caps recovered from the pits of the First Emperor's mausoleum record the trace Chu metalwork left in Qin equipment. The spark of revolt was also buried in the Chu country: in 208 BC Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu rose again in Jiangdong, and in 207 BC at Julu the Chu army won back the initiative against the main Qin force in open field, with an army and a hatred that Xiang Yan had sown.
result: 前224年是轉折：楚軍在秦軍追擊下於鄢、蘄一線崩潰，項燕兵敗，隨即傳出他自刭與被楚王遷所殺兩說，無論何者，楚軍在關鍵時刻失去主帥已是事實；楚王遷退保於陳，收攏殘兵再戰，於是次年兵敗。前223年王賁、蒙武分道追擊，攻平與、召陵，楚軍主力再次潰散，楚王遷被俘，部眾被驅往江南之地，楚國政權至此終結。項梁收拾項燕散卒，率之徙居江東，據會稽、吳中之地，數年後再起；這支由楚國舊卒與鄉里游兵組成的隊伍，成為前209年以後反秦序列的骨幹。楚地的統治則花了更久：前222年秦置黔中郡，王翦平定楚地亂軍，後以兵威掃清江南殘部，秦的郡縣制才真正在這一帶站穩腳跟。回頭看，這場戰爭真正的結局不是楚王遷的命運，而是六國並立的時代終結：秦以六十萬大軍、數百年的冶鐵與弩機技術，以及一次徹底的糧道決策，換來一個帝國的邊界；楚地人的抵抗則以另一種形式延續下去，直到秦末。
resultEn: The turn came in 224 BC: the Chu army collapsed under the Qin pursuit in the Yan and Qi area, Xiang Yan was beaten, and two accounts of his end have come down, that he killed himself and that the king of Chu had him killed; whichever is right, the fact remains that the Chu army lost its commander at the critical moment. King Qin fell back on Chen, gathered what was left of his troops and fought again, and was beaten the following year. In 223 BC Wang Ben and Meng Wu pursued in parallel, struck at Pingyu and Shaoling, the Chu army was scattered for the second time, King Qin was taken prisoner and his people were driven into the lands south of the river, and the government of Chu came to an end. Xiang Liang gathered the scattered men of Xiang Yan and moved with them to Jiangdong, establishing himself in the lands of Kuaiji and central Wu, and rose again a few years later; that force, built from the old soldiers of Chu and the local irregulars, became the backbone of the anti-Qin movement from 209 BC onward. Holding Chu territory took longer still: in 222 BC Qin established the commandery of Qianzhong, Wang Jian put down the rising in the Chu country, and the Qin order of commanderies and counties only took firm root in the region afterwards. Looking back, the real outcome of this war was not the fate of King Qin but the end of an age in which six states stood side by side. Qin bought the borders of an empire with 600,000 men, two centuries of ironworking and crossbow technology, and one thoroughly sound decision about supply; and the resistance of the people of Chu continued in another form, right into the last days of Qin.
